description: The primary flow of Bloxstrap begins with the Core Management & Configuration component initializing the environment and loading user-defined FastFlags. Control then passes to the Execution & Lifecycle Control component, which checks for existing instances via mutexes and initiates the Roblox launch sequence. During the game's execution, the Integration & Activity Monitoring component tracks the game process to update Discord Rich Presence and handle session-specific events. Throughout this process, the Localization & Resource Services and UI Presentation Utilities provide the necessary assets and data formatting to ensure the user interface remains responsive, localized, and visually consistent with the Windows desktop environment.

components.name: Lifecycle Orchestrator & Process Manager
components.description: The core engine of the subsystem that manages the execution flow. It handles process synchronization via mutexes, manages background updater lifecycles, and executes the primary Run loop that coordinates between the bootstrapper logic and the UI interface.

components_relations.evidence: The Orchestrator acts as the primary consumer of the Dialog Provider's factory methods. It requests specific IBootstrapperDialog implementations based on configuration (Fluent, Classic, etc.) and manages their visibility during the bootstrapper's execution loop.

components_relations.relation: Signals user intent and state changes
components_relations.evidence: The UI layer communicates back to the core engine via event callbacks and interface methods. Specifically, when a user closes a dialog or clicks cancel, the Provider triggers the Orchestrator's cancellation logic to halt process execution.

The Dialog Provider uses the Custom UI Engine as a specialized factory branch. When the user selects a 'Custom' style, the Provider hands off the XML/XAML parsing and object instantiation to the Engine to generate the WPF window.

components_relations.relation: Utilizes data transformation and error utilities
components_relations.evidence: The Custom UI Engine relies on the Orchestrator's utility layer for converting raw XML attributes (strings) into WPF-compatible types (Thickness, CornerRadius, etc.) and throws subsystem-specific exceptions managed by the Orchestrator.
